classes.name: Oral atypical antipsychotics
classes.description: Second-generation oral antipsychotics: aripiprazole, quetiapine IR/ER, olanzapine, risperidone, ziprasidone, lurasidone (Latuda), paliperidone ER, cariprazine (Vraylar), brexpiprazole (Rexulti), lumateperone (Caplyta), asenapine, iloperidone, clozapine, olanzapine/samidorphan (Lybalvi).
classes.plainDescription: A daily pill for schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or add-on treatment for depression.

classes.name: Long-acting injectable antipsychotics
classes.description: Long-acting injectables: aripiprazole (Abilify Maintena, Abilify Asimtufii, Aristada), paliperidone palmitate (Invega Sustenna/Trinza/Hafyera), risperidone (Risperdal Consta, Perseris, Uzedy, Rykindo), olanzapine pamoate (Zyprexa Relprevv), haloperidol and fluphenazine decanoate.
classes.plainDescription: A shot every few weeks or months instead of a daily pill.

preferredAgent.sig: Schizophrenia: 10-15 mg once daily. Bipolar mania: 15 mg once daily. Max 30 mg/day for both. Add-on for depression: start 2-5 mg once daily, max 15 mg/day. Dose per indication (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: One pill once a day; the dose depends on what it is treating.

records.verificationNote: Pick read directly: aripiprazole tablets are on the PREFERRED side of the Antipsychotics table (p.30); no PA printed for preferred agents. Chosen over quetiapine/risperidone/olanzapine only as a listed-first, commonly written generic; any preferred generic is defensible. PA criteria (p.29-31) apply to the non-preferred agents listed in paRequired. Lybalvi is a combination product, listed because the class description names it. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: Antipsychotics clinical PA is printed as applying to all drugs in the class (p.30); criteria not opened.]

preferredAgent.strength: 400 mg (standard maintenance strength; PDL does not print strength)
preferredAgent.sig: 400 mg IM (deltoid or gluteal) once monthly, no sooner than 26 days apart. Start with one 400 mg injection plus oral aripiprazole 10-20 mg daily for 14 days, or two 400 mg injections at separate sites plus one 20 mg oral dose; establish oral tolerability first (Abilify Maintena label).

records.verificationNote: Tier 1 and utilization flags for the risperidone 1 mg tablet read by x-coordinate on page 38 (tier column, then QL 60 per 30 days; no PA or ST). Risperidone ODT is step therapy and is listed under paRequired. Quantity limit on the 1 mg tablet is not a PA and is recorded here, not in preferredRestriction. Oral atypicals on pages 35-38. records.verificationNote: Tier and quantity-limit flags for the risperidone microspheres read by x-coordinate on page 38 (Tier 4, QL 2 per 28 days; no PA on any long-acting injectable on pages 35-38). Judgment: all long-acting options are Tier 4 with no PA, so the preferred pick is Risperdal Consta, a common product whose QL matches its every-2-week label dosing. Long-acting injectables are usually given in a clinic and may fall under the Part B medical benefit rather than Part D; the guide prints no BvsD flag on these rows, so the cost path is unconfirmed. Perseris, Uzedy and Rykindo do not appear in the guide. The guide does not state it is complete, so they are not recorded as excluded. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: Re-confirmed against Humana formulary 26402, v17 (updated 10/01/2026), sources/humana-premier-rx-pdp-newtopics-2026-10.pdf (tier, PA, ST, QL read by x-coordinate; the v16 copy used in the first pass is superseded). Risperdal Consta is Tier 4, QL 2 per 28 days, no PA on page 38. Sustenna is on pages 36-37, Trinza on 37, Hafyera on 36. Stays partial: no BvsD flag is printed, so the Part B or Part D path for clinic-given injections is unconfirmed.]
